verdict.rationale: Vercel Marketplace integrations for Postgres (Neon, Supabase, and others) and Redis (Upstash) provision stores with minimal setup and inject credentials and environment variables into the project, and Vercel Blob is first-party object storage with JS and Python SDKs. This reduces credential hand-wiring, but code still connects through provider SDKs using injected env vars rather than native runtime bindings, and a community report says secure database connectivity beyond a password requires Enterprise. Missing for 10: true native/runtime bindings that remove SDK boilerplate, a documented binding model for arbitrary external APIs, and hands-on corroboration of the low-boilerplate experience.

support.subject: As a developer, I can connect my code to external services like databases, APIs, and storage through native bindings with minimal boilerplate instead of hand-wiring SDKs and credentials

citations.quote: Provision and configure a Postgres database with minimal setup. Have credentials and environment variables injected into your Vercel project.

Vercel lets you connect external Redis databases through the Marketplace, allowing you to integrate high-performance caching and real-time data storage into your Vercel projects without managing Redis servers.
Vercel Blob is Vercel's object storage for files. Use it to store images, videos, documents, and other files your app uploads or serves.
A collection of first-party services you can easily add to your Vercel project.
